interactions.note: The structure of tAb2 Fab in complex with the epitope was determined from the crystal structure, solved by molecular replacement. There are two molecules in the crystallographic asymmetric unit. PDB chains for each complex are: Complex I (a) : Antibody heavy-chain: H, Antibody light-chain: L, epitope chain: P. Complex II (b) : Antibody heavy-chain: I, Antibody light-chain: M, epitope chain: Q. There are crystal contacts between the peptides and symmetry-related Fab molecules, but crystal packing had no measurable influence on the complex conformations. The C-terminus of the Fab heavy chain in complex (b) ends with I213, but in complex (a) it ends with P212 due to some disorder. Complex (b) was used in this analysis.; Unmapped quantitative response: 3D structure 1.9 angstroms

The binding of the epitope-specific tAb2 antibody and Fab fragment to the epitope was determined by isothermal calorimetry at 10, 25, and 35ºC. The value for the antibody in phosphate buffer at 25ºC is shown.; Unmapped quantitative response: association constant KA 0.0383 1/nM

The key residues for binding of the epitope-specific tAb2 antibody to the linear h-pep1 peptide were determined by substitutional analysis. Residues Asn 6 and Asp7 were most critical and could not be replaced by other amino acids.

The key residues for binding of the epitope-specific tAb2 antibody to the cyclized hc-pep1 peptide were determined by substitutional analysis. Residues Asn4 and Asp5 were most critical and could not be replaced by other amino acids, except Asp5 could be replaced by Glu. The peptide was cyclized by lactam formation between the N-terminal amino group of serine and the side chain carboxy group of the C-terminal glutamic acid.

The key residues for binding of the epitope-specific tAb2 antibody to the linear h-pep1 peptide were determined by substitutional analysis. Residues Asn5 and Asp6 were most critical. The peptide was cyclized by disulfide bond formation between the N-terminal and C-terminal cysteine residues.

The value for the antibody in phosphate buffer at 25ºC is shown. The peptide was cyclized by disulfide bond formation between the N-terminal and C-terminal cysteine residues.; Unmapped quantitative response: association constant KA 0.0067 1/nM

The structure of tAb2 Fab in complex with the cyclized hc-pep2 was determined from the crystal structure, solved by molecular replacement. Hc-pep2 is a cyclic peptide, homologous to an N-terminal epitope of TGFα. It was cyclized by lactam formation between the N-terminal amino group of serine and the side chain carboxy group of the C-terminal glutamic acid. The cyclization improves the peptide affinity to the antibody and the stability towards proteolysis.; Unmapped quantitative response: 3D structure 1.95 angstroms

The binding of the epitope-specific tAb2 antibody and Fab fragment to the cyclized hc-pep2 peptide was determined by isothermal calorimetry at 10, 25, and 35ºC. The value for the antibody in phosphate buffer at 25ºC is shown. The peptide was cyclized by lactam formation between the N-terminal amino group of serine and the side chain carboxy group of the C-terminal glutamic acid. The cyclization improves the peptide affinity to the antibody and the stability towards proteolysis. The linear peptide does not bind the tAb2 antibody, while the cyclized peptide binds the tAb2 with an affinity similar to that of the epitope.; Unmapped quantitative response: association constant KA 0.0392 1/nM

The epitope of Ly3016859 Fab on TGFα was determined from the crystal structure of the complex, solved by molecular replacement. The asymmetric unit contains two Fab and two TGFα molecules, which form a dimer through tetravalent coordination of a Zn2+ ion by the His18 and His35 side chains of TGFα.; Unmapped quantitative response: 3D structure 2.8 angstroms
